chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:
They evaluated the ring of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so my father took it from them for seven. I said, 'Seven dirhams?' He said, 'Seven dinars.'
ai.seo_question: How much did Imam al-Rida pay for his father's ring?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) purchasing his father Imam al-Sadiq’s ring for seven dinars, a transaction that underscores the spiritual and material reverence accorded to the Imams' personal effects. The specific mention of dinars (gold) rather than dirhams (silver) highlights the high status and purity associated with the Imam's seal, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tangible legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Safwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A ring of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was evaluated, so my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> took from it for seven’. I said, ‘Seven Dirhams?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seven Dinars’.
en.sarwar: 17. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Safwan who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
They evaluated the ring of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and my father bought it for seven.’ I then asked, ‘Was it seven dirham?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It was seven dinars.’”
